newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Sodra raises pulp price to $610/tonne.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Sodra raises pulp price to $610/tonne.

text.p: Swedish forestry cooperative Sodra said on Tuesday it raised softwood pulp prices to $610 per tonne from around $580.
Sodra spokesman Hans Burmeister told Reuters the decision was made on Thursday.

"In the United States several producers have announced increases to $630 per tonne for (softwood) pulp but it is slightly different quality and we felt that $610 was a price which better reflected market conditions," he said.
Pulp stockpiles among producers were low enough to justify pulp price increases, Burmeister said.
"The inventories as of the end of May were 1.6 million tonnes, which is low enough to move prices," he said.
"For some reason the market has decided that 1.5 million tonnes is a stock level which is a breaking point to move prices, but this is a figment of the imagination," said Burmeister.
